status_note: Versioned contract for the public USB Connector. The topic, ACL and envelope mapping below is the Backend's, relayed by its coder on 2026-11-19 for stage C3. Not yet verified against a real device or a real Backend: that is the C3 hardware leg.

sources.used_for: interface framing (0x7F), console line, one-request-at-a-time, id cache, limits
operation classes, USB cable as a transport
signed envelopes survive a bridge or broker; the unsigned USB cable caller
device-side MQTT behaviour the Connector mirrors: MQTT 3.1.1, clean session, retained status with last will, profile priority, cool-down, hold-down
established wrapper rules: marker, 16-bit length, MAX 176, resync
established console line and frame constants

transparency: never mints or substitutes identity; the topic root is configuration, not something read from the device
never holds keys, decrypts or rewrites a payload; it parses an uplink message only for its id, ev, epoch and usig members (routing and the enrolment gate)
never fabricates an acknowledgement; MQTT acceptance is not RF delivery and not Backend processing
never chooses a device or identity: one device, one configured topic root; the only choice it makes is the topic LEVEL (resp or ev/<ev>) under that root
device-signed envelopes are forwarded byte for byte

by: path: an explicit /dev/... path, normally a udev symlink such as /dev/bench/<name> (also --port <path> on the command line, which replaces the config selector)
vid + pid (+ optional usb serial number)
selection.path_rules: absolute, under /dev/, no wildcard or .., not a kernel tty node (/dev/ttyUSB*, /dev/ttyACM*, /dev/ttyS*, /dev/ttyAMA*, /dev/cu.*); it must resolve to a character device or it is polled like an absent stable id; no enumeration, so nothing else is ever a candidate
refused: a selector matching more than one port
selection.no_match: keep polling every 1 s; not an error
selection.mode_is_configured: companion or console; never auto-detected, because detection means reading payloads

wrapper.oversize_length: refused at once, rescan from the byte after the marker, never buffered
wrapper.checksum: none; corruption inside a plausible length cannot be detected

classification.action: reassemble by (xid, index, count) and forward the message
drop and count; native Companion traffic is not forwarded

mecon_frame.repeated_frame: ignored; frames of the last completed (xid, count) are ignored until another xid arrives

downlink.wrap: marker 0x3C, then one 0x7F frame per 168 bytes, xid from one Connector counter 1..255 then 0, shared with the enrolment request (which takes xid 1)
downlink.note: a request longer than the device's hello limits.rx_bytes can be cut by a busy UART; the operator sets max_downlink_bytes to stay inside it

console.skipped: echo, log lines and stock CLI replies; skipped as soon as the line is known not to be an interface line, never buffered
console.oversize_line: refused without buffering; the rest of the line is discarded up to its terminator
console.published_bytes: the line after the 7-byte prefix, terminator removed, nothing else changed

downlink.wrap: mecon> + message + CR in one write
downlink.refused: a message containing CR or LF (it would split into several console lines)

serial.stall_behaviour: a partial frame with no new byte for stall_s is dropped and counted; the stream resynchronises on the next marker
serial.unplug: close the port, drop partial frames, publish connector status serial=down, poll for the same stable id; nothing is replayed after a replug

tls.default: required with peer verification and host-name check, TLS 1.2 or newer
tls.plain: refused unless a broker sets insecure_allow_plain = true (loopback or a closed test LAN)
tls.failure: fail closed: no downgrade to plain, no unverified TLS, no connection

topic_root.source: configuration; provisioned by the party that provisions the broker login
topic_root.shape: mecon/<device_id>, where device_id is the device's own 16-byte id as 32 lowercase hex digits (^[0-9a-f]{32}$), as reported by hello and deployment.get. The Connector never reads it from the device: the operator copies it into the config.
topic_root.rules: plain levels of A-Za-z0-9._- ; no wildcard, no leading slash, no $

login.note: The Connector publishes and subscribes only on those topics, so a login with exactly this ACL is enough. The ACL is the Backend's; the Connector never relies on it for its own safety rules.

resp.carries: a device-to-host message that answers a request: it has an `id` member (and no `ev`). One MQTT message per envelope, payload byte for byte, with the device's own usig signature.

ev.carries: a device-to-host event: it has an `ev` member naming the stream (inventory, health, power, radio, runtime, rf, message, ...). Published to {topic_root}/ev/<that name>, payload byte for byte, with the device's own usig signature.
ev.ev_name_rule: ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$; any other value (a slash, a wildcard, empty, not a string) has no route

req.carries: host-to-device requests, one MQTT message per envelope: the Backend's signed envelope, passed through unchanged
req.retained_messages: refused and counted; the Backend never retains a request
req.opens_when: the enrolment gate is open (see enrolment_gate); there is no configuration switch
req.while_closed: messages are refused and counted (downlink_closed_total), never held, never replayed

status.carries: the Connector's own transport state: online is true only while the broker session is up AND the device's serial port is open. It never stands for the device's identity, health, enrolment or radio presence.
published_on: clean shutdown ({"online":false}, the same bytes as the will)
status.decision: The retained status and the will share the Backend's shape {"online":...}, so one consumer reads both. The Connector's earlier detail payload (connector and serial members) is dropped from the topic; serial state remains in /healthz and /metrics.

routing.decision: The Connector chooses only the TOPIC from the parsed envelope. The bytes published are the device's own bytes, never re-serialised, never signed, never given a wrapper.
rules: an `ev` member that is a safe name (ev_name_rule) -> {topic_root}/ev/<ev>
no `ev` and an `id` that is a non-empty string or an integer -> {topic_root}/resp

anything else (no id and no ev, an unsafe or non-string ev, id empty/null/boolean, JSON that is not an object, or bytes that are not JSON) -> no route: dropped and counted as upstream_dropped_total{reason="unroutable"}, never published and never guessed. An unsafe ev never falls back to resp.
routing.already_parsed: The enrolment gate already parses every uplink message for id, epoch and usig; routing reads two more members of the same parse.
routing.unchanged_bytes: Nothing is added or removed. The Connector does not verify, rewrite or re-sign: a Connector that rewrote an answer or event would break its usig signature.

client_id.rule: configured, 1-64 chars of A-Za-z0-9._- ; never generated or derived from the device
client_id.note: two sessions with one id make the broker evict the older one

brokers.order: list order is priority; first is primary, the rest are fallbacks
brokers.active: exactly one session at a time
brokers.selection: the first broker not cooling down
brokers.return_to_better: after the session on a fallback is at least hold_down_s old and a better broker is not cooling down, close and reconnect to the better one; at most one switch per hold-down

reconnect.owner: the Connector decides when and where to reconnect; the MQTT library never reconnects or replays on its own

enrolment_gate.decision: Downlink opens only while the device itself reports an enrolled Deployment record, and fails closed on anything else. An unenrolled device gets uplink only. Owner decision, 2026-11-18.

request.class: read, open to the unsigned cable on every role
request.framing: the active one: 0x7F frames in companion mode, one `mecon> ` line in console mode

enrolment_gate.open_only_when: reply status is ok and result.state is "provisioned"

classification.note: Draft 2. The firmware answers deployment.get with status ok, busy (no memory) or failed (storage). busy and failed say nothing about the record, so neither is read as not provisioned. Every answer whose status is not ok is logged as a warning (gate_probe_not_ok) with its status and error code only, never the usig or the result body.
classification.provisioned: status ok and result.state provisioned: open; ask again after recheck_s. Ends a run of failed answers.
classification.none_or_corrupt: status ok and result.state none or corrupt: close at once (reason not_provisioned); ask again after retry_s. Counted none or corrupt.
classification.malformed: status ok without a readable result.state, or with another state: close at once (reason not_provisioned). Counted malformed.
classification.busy: status busy: nothing changes by itself (an open gate stays open, a closed one stays closed; queued downlink and a hold are kept). Counted busy. The first busy_backoff_after (default 3) busy answers in a row are asked again after busy_retry_s; from the next one on, after retry_s. A busy answer neither adds to nor ends a run of failed answers, except as the next rule says. When no decided answer (provisioned, none, corrupt, malformed, refused) has come for more than twice recheck_s, counted from the last decided answer or, if there has been none, from the opening of the serial port, each further busy answer counts as one failed answer (below) and is asked again after retry_s. Twice, because the first recheck is already due at recheck_s: the window the Connector accepts without a fresh answer is that one, and a further recheck_s of only busy answers exceeds it.
classification.busy_log: The first busy answer of a run is logged as a warning (gate_probe_not_ok, fields status and error only); later busy answers of the same run as debug lines. When the run ends (a decided answer, a failed answer, or the gate closing for any reason) one info line gate_probe_busy_run_ended with the field count (the busy answers in the run) is logged. A run ends and a new window starts with a decided answer or a newly opened serial port.
classification.failed: status failed: counted failed; ask again after retry_s. The gate closes (reason probe_failed) only at failed_threshold failed answers in a row; fewer change nothing. Reaching the threshold closes the gate and, on the hold transport, releases the hold, exactly as an answer that says the device is not enrolled does. Any decided answer (provisioned, none, corrupt, malformed, refused, timeout) and a newly opened serial port start the count again. Every failed answer is logged as a warning.
classification.refused: any other status, or none: a real refusal; close at once (reason not_provisioned). Counted refused.

closed_when: a status other than ok, busy or failed
failed_threshold failed answers in a row (busy answers past twice recheck_s count as failed)
an answer that does not parse or has another state
an uplink interface message without a usig member
ask_when: an epoch different from the last one is seen
the first unsigned uplink message closes an open gate
every retry_s after a failed answer below failed_threshold
busy_retry_s after each of the first busy_backoff_after busy answers in a row (default 3, 1-60), then retry_s
enrolment_gate.inspection: Only: the Connector's own reply (matched by its request id), whether the top-level usig member is present, and an epoch (top-level epoch, result.epoch or usig_boot). Nothing else is read. Uplink is never altered and forwarded to the topic its envelope routes to (routing), except the device's reply to the Connector's own request.
enrolment_gate.own_traffic_upstream: The request is never published upstream and the reply to it is not published upstream: they are the Connector's traffic, not device-originated. The protocol does not require them upstream. Replies are matched by the reserved id prefix cg-; a late reply is dropped and counted (result late).
enrolment_gate.unsigned_rule: While a record exists every interface event and result ends with usig_boot, usig_seq and usig. The first uplink 0x7F or `mecon> {` message with no usig closes downlink at once, because that is what follows a deployment.reset. It reopens only after a fresh deployment.get says provisioned. Native Companion frames are not interface messages and never count.
enrolment_gate.downlink_content: No signature or operation check on relayed content: for an enrolled device the firmware requires a member's signature for everything but reads, and the owner decided unsigned reads are relayed too. The broker ACL on req stays a further layer.
enrolment_gate.one_request_at_a_time: The firmware handles one interface message at a time. The Connector's request can interleave with a Backend request that is in flight; a Backend that gets a busy answer re-sends with the same id.
enrolment_gate.xid: The request is the first message written after the port opens (xid 1), so the first relayed message uses xid 2.

retry_rules.rule: new session on a new client object, with backoff
every 1 s while the stable id is absent or the open fails

retry_rules.what: upstream envelope queued and never handed to the broker
retry_rules.rule: sent after reconnect, in order, until upstream_ttl_s; this is its first send

retry_rules.what: upstream publish handed to the broker with no PUBACK when the session ended
retry_rules.rule: counted as upstream_uncertain and forgotten; the broker may already hold it
written to the serial port at most once; never held across a serial unplug, a TTL of downlink_ttl_s, or a restart
counted as downlink_write_failed; the device may have seen all, part or none of it
state, not an event; republished on every connect and change

delivery.why_no_replay: a device command repeated by an intermediary is a duplicate business action. The firmware keeps an id cache, but only for state-changing operations and only for a bounded number of ids, and a Backend may have signed the request once. Recovery belongs to the sender: it re-sends with the same id and reads the result.
delivery.duplicates_upstream: QoS 1 can deliver a message twice at the broker. The Connector adds none of its own. Envelopes carry (epoch, seq) or a request id; the Backend de-duplicates by those, which the Connector does not read.
delivery.ordering: upstream envelopes keep the order the device sent them in, per session; across a lost publish there is a gap, never a reorder
never: write a command while the enrolment gate is closed
hold a refused command for when the gate reopens
publish an envelope the device did not send
write a command the broker did not deliver

upstream.full: drop the newest envelope and count it (upstream_dropped_total reason queue_full); queued envelopes keep their place

downlink.full: drop the newest and count it (reason queue_full)
downlink.serial_down: dropped and counted at once (reason serial_down)

queues.serial_read: no queue: bytes are consumed as they arrive; every reader is bounded by its frame limit
queues.backpressure: none towards the device. A full queue drops and counts. The device's own bounded transmit queue and frame gate decide what the device does when the host is slow.
queues.silent_drops: forbidden: every drop increments a metric

health.http: GET /healthz (200 when serial is up and a broker session is established, else 503) and GET /metrics, bound to 127.0.0.1 by default
health.ready_means: the two transport links are up; it says nothing about the device, the Backend or RF

errors.condition: the device is not known to be enrolled, or its state cannot be read
errors.behaviour: refuse downlink and count it (downlink_closed_total); uplink continues; ask again

errors.condition: an open gate and an uplink interface message with no usig
errors.behaviour: close downlink at once, forward the message unchanged, ask deployment.get
poll every 1 s; serial_connected 0; not fatal
refuse to open any; poll every 5 s; log once
close, drop partial frames, status serial=down, reopen on the same selector

errors.condition: interface line above 1607 bytes (a 1600-byte message after the prefix)
partial frame, no byte for stall_s

errors.behaviour: backoff, then the next broker; queue within bounds
fail closed, long cool-down, no publish

errors.condition: session ended with an unacknowledged publish
empty, too large, retained, or CR/LF in console mode

errors.behaviour: refuse to start, exit 2, list every problem

open_questions.question: One up topic for results and events; the Connector cannot split them without reading the payload. Does the Backend de-multiplex?
open_questions.answer: Yes (Backend, 2026-11-18). The Backend parses each message by its own shape. Keep the bytes untouched: the usig signature is checked over them. Superseded in shape by the Backend's mapping of 2026-11-19: the Connector now splits the single up topic into resp and ev/<ev> from the parsed envelope (routing), bytes unchanged.

open_questions.question: A relayed write arrives as the unsigned local cable caller.
open_questions.answer: Owner decision, 2026-11-18: downlink is relayed only while the device reports an enrolled Deployment record, and fails closed otherwise (enrolment_gate). Unsigned reads are relayed too for an enrolled device; there is no signature check on downlink content. Still to confirm with mecon-firmware before stage C3: whether an enrolled device accepts any unsigned read that returns data the Backend alone should see.

open_questions.question: Dual transport arbitration and duplicate events.
open_questions.answer: The Backend de-duplicates by (device, stream, epoch, seq) after the signature verifies, and sends a request over the path that currently holds the device. The holder must release cleanly: the Connector publishes its status offline and closes the broker session on shutdown. Gap counting across transports is a Backend gap, tracked on their side.

open_questions.question: Does a Companion's USB serial accept 0x7F frames before the app handshake, and does boot-time text ever precede frames on every USB build? Not answered by the Backend mapping: it is device behaviour, observed by the C3 hardware run (the Connector's first write is deployment.get, with no handshake).
Should native (non-0x7F) Companion frames be forwarded?
open_questions.answer: No (mecon-firmware, 2026-11-18). Downlink they would run at cable trust (CLI command frame, native key export and import, set-PIN, factory reset); uplink they carry private messages. Dropped and counted both ways.

open_questions.question: Is the Connector status topic wanted, and under what name?
open_questions.answer: Yes (Backend coder, 2026-11-19): {topic_root}/status, retained, QoS 0, last will {"online":false} retained on the same topic. The Connector's own detail topic {topic_root}/connector/status is gone: the login's ACL allows exactly resp, status and ev/+ for publish. Payload decision: the Backend's {"online":...} shape wins over the earlier connector/serial payload, because it is the single shape the Backend and the will already share and the ACL leaves no second topic for the detail; online means broker session up and serial port open, never device presence.
